analysis:
This PR adds a changelog entry (changelog.d/mixed-step-prefill-chunk.md) and a documentation paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 549-567). No executable code is in the supplied batch; the actual geometry change (EngineV2Factory.usesWidePrefillChunk in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift) is not visible here, so the code behavior is an unverified contract.

The docs describe Gemma 4 moving to 2,048-token prefill chunks with a 4,096-token step budget during mixed decode steps. Media requests keep 512-token chunks. GPT-OSS, dense Qwen, MoE Qwen and other families stay at 512/2,048 by default. The docs claim no change to KV grants, load quotations, ring sizes or activation floors, and say the Gemma peak (3.73 GiB) fits inside the 5.5 GiB reserve.

The docs also disclose that GPT-OSS (3.62 vs 3.5 GiB floor) and Qwen3.5-9B (6.03 vs 5.5 GiB) already exceed their floors at eight 32k-token prompts, even under the previous geometry. That is a documented, pre-existing availability and memory-headroom gap. It is not introduced here, because those families keep the old geometry by default. The opt-in env overrides (DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK / DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS) are operator-local, and the changelog says they disqualify reviewed serving profiles. Operators already control the provider process, so this is consistent with TB-003 and ADV-001 and adds no new trust boundary.

Threat-model relevance is limited to memory-availability posture (T-016, T-029), and no changes to encryption, attestation, the authorization path or prefix-cache storage (T-041) appear. Open question for the code pass: confirm that Gemma's 4,096-token mixed step really stays within the activation reserve and that media requests really fall back to 512-token chunks. I cannot verify that from docs alone. No qualifying finding.
